positions.commentary: Bank of America believes the drug shortage will resolve, the company cannot compound the drug, revenue will decline, and the stock price will drop within the fiscal year.

thesis: This episode argues that Bank of America faces revenue decline and a stock price drop within the fiscal year due to an unresolved drug shortage and the company's inability to compound the drug. Additionally, the speaker advocates shorting BLSH, citing an inability to legally or practically manufacture compounds at scale and a shift from optimistic sell-side to pessimistic buy-side views.

claims.claim: Bank of America believes the drug shortage will resolve, the company cannot compound the drug, revenue will decline, and the stock price will drop within the fiscal year.
claims.quote: Bank of America has basically said this drug is going to come off. They are not going to be able to compound it. They are not going to be able to make as much money as they used to and the stock is going to drop. Again, they didn't even highlight when it could happen and it said within this fiscal year, it will happen and it will take, it will take its toll on the company's stock price.

claims.claim: The speaker states they are short BLSH because they believe the company cannot legally or practically manufacture the compounds at scale, noting a shift from optimistic sell-side to pessimistic buy-side views.
claims.quote: So on the buy side, it was very pessimistic. Yeah, I was like, no, we're short. Like, do you call somebody? I'm like, no, we're short. We don't think it's going to happen either. So it was a very big shift between publicly from sell side being optimistic and then privately from buy side agreeing with me saying there's no shot.
